newsitem.title: USA: U.S. manufacturers urge Fed to accommodate growth.
newsitem.headline: U.S. manufacturers urge Fed to accommodate growth.

text.p: A group representing U.S. manufacturers on Wednesday urged the Federal Reserve to leave interest rates unchanged in order to accommodate growth.

"The best course of action for the Federal Reserve (would be to) simply leave interest rates the way they are," said Gordon Richards, economist for the National Association of Manufacturers, in prepared testimony to the House Banking Committee.
Richards said structual changes in labor and product markets make it possible for the economy to keep expanding at a healthy clip without spurring inflation.
"As a result of structural changes during the 1990s, the economy can now achieve faster growth with continued low inflation.
U.S. gross domestic product grew by 5.9 percent in the first quarter of this year, a surge Richards attributed to "a whole series of one-time factors."
He said his group expects the expansion to slow to a rate of 2.5 percent to 3 percent during the second half of 1997. Such a rate is close to the economy's long-run potential but not above it.
The manufacturers group looks for growth of 3 percent or higher for 1997 as a whole.
